papers.title: ISUP Grade Group Migration Between Prostate Biopsy and Radical Prostatectomy: A Systematic Review of Emerging Predictors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group discordance between prostate biopsy and radical prostatectomy (RP) affects 25-50% of men with localized prostate cancer and has direct implications for active surveillance, nerve-sparing, and adjuvant-treatment decisions. We synthesized contemporary evidence on the frequency of biopsy-to-RP grade migration and on emerging imaging, molecular/genomic, and artificial-intelligence (AI)-based predictors of migration. Methods: MEDLINE (PubMed) was searched from 1 January 2010 to 5 May 2026, supplemented by citati
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on ISUP Grade Group discordance between prostate biopsy and radical prostatectomy, which occurs in 25-50% of men and affects treatment decisions. It highlights emerging imaging, molecular/genomic, and AI-based predictors that may help identify patients at risk for grade migration.

papers.title: AI-Guided Long Non-Coding RNA Target Discovery for Precision Medicine: Integrating GWAS, Multi-Omics, Experimental Validation, and RNA Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Precision medicine requires translation of genetic and molecular variation into clinically actionable therapeutic targets. However, many disease-associated signals identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) reside in non-coding regulatory regions, making biological interpretation and therapeutic prioritization difficult. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules with growing relevance to disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and RNA-based therapeutics. This review presents a translational framework for AI-guided lncRNA t
papers.summary: This review proposes a translational framework that integrates GWAS, multi-omics data, experimental validation, and RNA therapeutics with AI-guided approaches to identify and prioritize long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as therapeutic targets for precision medicine. It highlights the challenges of interpreting non-coding disease-associated variants and outlines how AI can help bridge the gap from genetic signals to clinically actionable lncRNA targets.

papers.title: DyAb: sequence-based antibody design and property prediction in a low-data regime.
papers.abstract: Protein therapeutic design and property prediction are frequently hampered by data scarcity. Here we propose a model, DyAb, that addresses these issues by leveraging a pair-wise representation to predict differences in binding affinity, rather than absolute values. DyAb is built on top of a pre-trained protein language model and achieves a Spearman rank correlation of up to 0.85 on binding affinity prediction across monoclonal antibodies targeting three different antigens (EGFR, IL-6, and an internal target), given as few as 100 training data. We employ DyAb in two design contexts: as a rankin
papers.summary: DyAb is a new sequence-based model for antibody design and property prediction that works well even with limited data. By predicting differences in binding affinity rather than absolute values, and building on a pre-trained protein language model, it achieves high accuracy (Spearman correlation up to 0.85) with as few as 100 training examples across multiple antibody targets. The model is useful for ranking antibody variants in design workflows.

papers.title: Learning precise segmentation of neurofibrillary tangles from rapid manual point annotations.
papers.abstract: Accumulation of abnormal tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) is a pathologic hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD). Accurate detection of NFTs in tissue samples can reveal relationships with clinical, demographic, and genetic features through deep phenotyping. However, expert manual analysis is time-consuming, subject to observer variability, and cannot handle the data amounts generated by modern imaging. We present a scalable, open-source, deep-learning approach to quantify NFT burden in digital whole slide images (WSIs) of post-mortem human brain tissue. To achieve this, we develope
papers.summary: This paper presents an open-source deep-learning method for automatically segmenting neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in whole slide images of Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, trained using rapid manual point annotations instead of time-consuming pixel-level tracing. The approach enables scalable and consistent quantification of NFT burden, which can support deep phenotyping studies linking pathology to clinical and genetic data.

papers.title: scProtoTransformer: Scalable reference mapping across molecules, cells, and donors.
papers.abstract: The rapid accumulation of single-cell data has made it possible to comprehensively characterize biological systems at molecular, cellular, and donor levels. However, scalable reference mapping across different resolutions remains a major challenge in current research. Here, we propose scProtoTransformer, a prototype-based Transformer architecture designed to achieve scalable reference mapping across molecular, cell, and donor levels. scProtoTransformer introduces a knowledge-guided prototype tokenizer that projects gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes, effectively
papers.summary: scProtoTransformer is a new Transformer-based method that enables scalable mapping of single-cell data across molecular, cellular, and donor levels by using a knowledge-guided prototype tokenizer to project gene expression into interpretable pathway prototypes. This approach addresses the challenge of cross-resolution reference mapping in large-scale single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Programmable protein degraders enable selective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin subpopulations in vitro and in vivo.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of Wnt signaling results in unregulated accumulation of cytosolic β-catenin, which subsequently enters the nucleus and promotes transcription of genes that contribute to cellular proliferation and malignancy. Here, we sought to eliminate pathogenic β-catenin from the cytosol using designer ubiquibodies (uAbs), chimeric proteins composed of an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target-binding domain that redirect intracellular proteins to the proteasome for degradation. To accelerate uAb development, we leveraged a protein language model-driven algorithm called SaLT&PepPr to computat
papers.summary: The authors developed programmable protein degraders called ubiquibodies (uAbs) that selectively eliminate pathogenic cytosolic β-catenin, a key driver of Wnt-driven cancers. Using a protein language model-driven algorithm (SaLT&PepPr) to design the targeting domain, they demonstrated effective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin in vitro and in vivo, offering a new therapeutic strategy for Wnt-addicted cancers.

papers.title: iDCF: Interpretable deconvolution of cell fractions via biologically-informed deep learning using scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Precise resolution of cellular heterogeneity within complex tissues is fundamental to deciphering disease etiologies from bulk transcriptomic profiles. While computational deconvolution offers a scalable alternative, current deep learning methods predominantly operate as "black boxes," neglecting the structural constraints of biological laws. This reliance on purely data-driven feature extraction often yields biologically incoherent predictions and limited mechanistic interpretability. iDCF (Interpretable Deconvolution of Cell Fractions) is a novel framework that enforces biological topology o
papers.summary: iDCF is a new deep learning framework for deconvolving cell fractions from bulk transcriptomics that explicitly incorporates biological structural constraints, improving interpretability and biological coherence over black-box methods. It leverages scRNA-seq data to inform the model architecture, yielding more reliable cell-type proportion estimates.

papers.title: Deciphering the comprehensive relationship between 5' UTR and 3' UTR sequences with deep learning.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in mRNA therapeutics have driven further research on the untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA. However, prior studies have mainly focused on either the 5' or 3' UTR individually. Increasing evidence suggests potential cooperative effects between these two regions, which remain largely unexplored in computational studies.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning approach to jointly analyze 5' and 3' UTR sequences, revealing cooperative effects between these regions that influence mRNA function. The model captures combined regulatory signals, offering a more comprehensive framework for understanding UTR-mediated gene regulation and aiding mRNA therapeutic design.

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities in type III secretion system effector prediction.
papers.abstract: Type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs) are small bacterial proteins with big biological roles. They act as central molecular mediators of interactions between Gram-negative bacteria and eukaryotic hosts, spanning pathogenic, symbiotic and environmental contexts. Over the past three decades, T3SE discovery has progressed from genome-independent experimental assays to an expanding landscape of computational prediction methods. Early in silico approaches formalized empirically defined protein N-terminal properties into feature-engineered machine-learning models, followed by deep-learning met
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolution of computational methods for predicting type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs), from early feature-engineered machine learning models to modern deep-learning approaches. It highlights ongoing challenges in accurate prediction and outlines opportunities for future methodological improvements.

papers.title: Development of a Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-Interpretable Model for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Implications of MDA-Modified Protein Adducts and Autoantibodies.
papers.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study explores the two-hit oxidative-immune hypothesis by evaluating malondialdehyde (MDA)-modified protein (MDA-protein) adducts and their corresponding autoantibodies for precise and fair CAD severity stratification and classification. Novel MDA-peptide epitopes (apolipoprotein B-100 (ApoB-100), fibronectin (FINC), and complement C4A/C4B (C4A/C4B)) were identified via proteomics, and plasma levels of MDA, adducts, and autoantibodies were measured in 165 Taiwanese T2DM patients. Multivaria
papers.summary: This study developed a SHAP-interpretable machine learning model to stratify coronary artery disease severity in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients using malondialdehyde-modified protein adducts and their autoantibodies. The authors identified novel MDA-peptide epitopes via proteomics and measured plasma levels in 165 patients, demonstrating the potential of oxidative-immune biomarkers for precise and fair CAD risk classification.

papers.title: CompBio and MIRaS-a multi-omic analysis platform built on a memory-based intelligence engine.
papers.abstract: As molecular and cellular technologies have advanced, the need to analyze and interpret the resulting vast and multi-modal data into actionable intelligence has become a rate-limiting factor in scientific advancement. While traditional knowledgebase-pathway tools and LLM-based AI tools provide a degree of support in data interpretation, both exhibit known limitations. Presented here is the CompBio multi-omic analysis platform built upon Memory-based Intelligent Reasoning System (MIRaS), an associative reasoning engine grounded in episodic and semantic memory, capable of inferring biological re
papers.summary: The authors present CompBio, a multi-omic analysis platform built on MIRaS, a memory-based reasoning engine that uses episodic and semantic memory to infer biological relationships from complex datasets. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional pathway tools and LLM-based AI in interpreting multi-modal molecular data.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review discusses recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges: cross-domain distribution shifts, relational mismatches, and feature heterogeneity. It surveys three AI paradigms that address these barriers and examines their clinical translation potential.

papers.title: GRASSP: RNA Language Model-Enhanced Graph Attention with Adaptive Gating for RNA-Small Molecule Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA-small molecule binding site prediction is crucial for targeted drug discovery. Sequence-based methods are efficient but often fail to capture structural dependencies between nucleotides, whereas structure-aware graph models can better represent spatial interactions but typically rely on complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing pipelines. We therefore developed GRASSP, a streamlined hybrid deep learning framework that integrates pretrained RNA language model (LM) representations with adaptive graph refinement.
papers.summary: GRASSP is a new deep learning framework that combines RNA language model embeddings with graph neural networks to predict RNA-small molecule binding sites. It improves accuracy by capturing structural dependencies without requiring complex structural annotations or multi-stage preprocessing, offering a streamlined approach for targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: Publisher Correction: FeatureDock for protein-ligand docking guided by physicochemical feature-based local environment learning using transformer.
papers.summary: This is a publisher correction notice for a previously published article, not a new research finding. It likely corrects minor errors in the original paper, so it does not contribute new scientific knowledge.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings and genomic-neighborhood features to fill gaps in functional annotations of carbohydrate metabolism genes in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high cross-validation performance (F1-macro 84.64%) and improved coverage of carbohydrate-active enzyme annotations, enabling more complete metabolic interpretation.

papers.title: An Integrated Consensus Machine Learning and Structure-Based Workflow for the Discovery of Novel Tankyrase 1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background: Tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) is a poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase involved in Wnt/β-catenin signaling, telomere maintenance, and genomic stability, making it an attractive therapeutic target in oncology. This study aimed to develop and apply an integrated computational workflow to identify novel TNKS1 inhibitor candidates. Methods: A curated dataset of experimentally validated TNKS1 inhibitors and property-matched DUD-E decoys was used to develop a consensus supervised machine learning (ML) model prioritization framework for ligand-based virtual screening, integrating Morgan fingerprints with t
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational workflow combining consensus machine learning with structure-based methods to discover novel Tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) inhibitors, a promising oncology target. The approach uses curated experimental data and decoys to build a ligand-based virtual screening model, successfully identifying new candidate inhibitors.

papers.title: Integrated AI-Driven Discovery of MAPK3 Inhibitors for Oral Inflammatory and Proliferative Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 (MAPK3/ERK1) plays a central role in cellular proliferation, inflammation, apoptosis, and survival signalling and has been implicated in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), periodontitis, oral lichen planus, and other chronic oral inflammatory diseases. The present study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and MM-GBSA analysis to identify and characte
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated AI-driven computational workflow—combining machine learning-based QSAR modeling, molecular docking, DFT, molecular dynamics, and MM-GBSA—to identify and characterize potential MAPK3 (ERK1) inhibitors for oral inflammatory and proliferative diseases. The approach successfully pinpoints promising drug candidates, offering a novel strategy for targeting MAPK3 in conditions like oral squamous cell carcinoma and periodontitis.

papers.title: Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms in Distant Kinship Inference and Forensic Genetic Genealogy.
papers.abstract: Forensic genetics is moving from locus-based DNA profiling toward genome-wide inference enabled by high-density single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data. While short tandem repeats remain central to routine human identification, SNP-based technologies and massively parallel sequencing have expanded the analysis of distant kinship through detection of identity-by-descent (IBD) segments and shared autosomal DNA. This narrative review synthesizes the biological basis of SNP-based distant kinship inference, the statistical and computational frameworks used to model genomic relatedness, and the op
papers.summary: This review discusses the shift in forensic genetics from traditional STR profiling to genome-wide SNP analysis for distant kinship inference, focusing on identity-by-descent segment detection and computational modeling. It synthesizes the biological and statistical frameworks underpinning SNP-based relatedness estimation, highlighting its applications in forensic genetic genealogy.

papers.title: SEFA: Semantic Embedding-Based Feature Augmentation of Biomedical Language-Model Embeddings Improves Interpretable Metabolomic Prediction of Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Feature engineering remains a major challenge in metabolomics-based prediction, particularly when rich biochemical knowledge is available but underutilized. Conventional metabolomics models rely primarily on measured variables and statistically driven feature selection, overlooking the molecular and pathway context encoded in curated metabolite knowledge bases. We propose SEFA (Semantic Embedding-based Feature Augmentation), a model-agnostic framework that integrates metabolite-level textual knowledge from the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) into structured metabolomics
papers.summary: SEFA is a new framework that augments metabolomics data with semantic embeddings from the Human Metabolome Database, improving interpretable prediction of lung cancer. By incorporating biochemical knowledge into machine learning models, it outperforms conventional feature selection and provides more biologically meaningful insights.

papers.title: Exploratory Biological Correlates of Cognitive and Language Performance in Healthy Pubertal Children: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adolescence is a dynamic neurodevelopmental period during which structured language performance may reflect ongoing biological reorganization processes. This study examined whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers were modestly associated with structured language task performance and cognitive performance in healthy pubertal children. Methods: A total of 156 healthy pubertal children (78 female, 78 male; mean age of 11.84 ± 2.98 years) meeting Tanner Stage ≥ 2 were included in this retrospective cross-sectional study. Language was assessed with the Test
papers.summary: This study explored whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers are associated with cognitive and language performance in healthy pubertal children, finding modest correlations that suggest biological factors may play a role in neurodevelopment during adolescence. The findings are preliminary and warrant further investigation.

papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow.
papers.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation. BioMaster incorporates a dual retrieval-augmented design to leverage domain knowledge for tool selection, parameterization, and adaptation across tasks. A dedicated debug
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent framework that automates complex bioinformatics workflows by integrating planning, execution, error recovery, and validation. It uses a dual retrieval-augmented design to improve tool selection and parameterization, addressing robustness issues in LLM-based agents for multi-step analyses.

papers.title: Brain-AI convergence: Generative world models and hierarchical attention for human intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI provide new insights into how the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, support diverse functions and human intelligence. Beyond the traditional focus on visual processing, this paper offers a cross-domain comparison of the brain and AI through the lens of world-model-based computation. We argue that both the neocortex and cerebellum predict future world states from past inputs and construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning. These predictive world models are repurposed for sensory comprehension and
papers.summary: This paper proposes that the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, function as generative world models that predict future states through prediction-error learning, a principle mirrored in modern AI. It offers a cross-domain comparison suggesting that hierarchical attention mechanisms in AI can inform our understanding of human intelligence and brain function.

papers.title: Systematic Screening of Depression-Related Neurotoxicity Across 26 Bisphenols Reveals an ESR1-CREB1-GRIN2B-Associated Mechanism.
papers.abstract: Bisphenols (BPs) are widespread environmental endocrine disruptors, but their potential depression-related neurotoxicity has not been systematically assessed. Here, we combined machine learning (ML), network toxicology, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments to screen 26 bisphenols for depression-related neurotoxic risk. We first integrated bisphenol A (BPA)-related targets with depression-related genes to build a chemical-gene-phenotype-disease network and an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework. We then used nine ML algorithms to rank the predicted risk of the 26 bisphenols. Molecular
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluated 26 bisphenols for depression-related neurotoxicity using machine learning, network toxicology, and in vivo experiments, identifying an ESR1-CREB1-GRIN2B-associated mechanism. The findings suggest that certain bisphenols may pose depression risks through this pathway, providing a framework for prioritizing hazardous compounds.

papers.title: GAMT-GINE: A Graph Isomorphism Network Integrating Continuous Spatial Awareness and Multi-Task Learning for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand interactions (PLIs) play a crucial role in drug discovery, and accurately predicting protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) remains a central challenge in computer-aided drug design. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated considerable potential in molecular modeling, existing methods still face several limitations, including excessive reliance on hand-crafted chemical features, loss of spatial information, and difficulties in integrating heterogeneous affinity labels, which restrict their generalization capability in PLA prediction. To address these challenges, w
papers.summary: This paper introduces GAMT-GINE, a graph isomorphism network that integrates continuous spatial awareness and multi-task learning to improve protein-ligand binding affinity prediction. The method addresses limitations of existing GNNs, such as reliance on hand-crafted features and loss of spatial information, and demonstrates enhanced generalization capability.

papers.title: AI-Supported Prediction of Vesicoureteral Reflux in Children Based on Cystoscopic Configuration of the Ureteric Orifice.
papers.abstract: Background: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is a common pediatric urological disorder traditionally diagnosed by voiding cystourethrography (VCUG). Although ureteric orifice (UO) morphology during cystoscopy correlates with VUR severity, its assessment remains subjective. To our knowledge, artificial intelligence (AI) has not previously been applied to cystoscopic images for VUR prediction. We aimed to develop and evaluate the first AI model for predicting VUR from pediatric cystoscopic images and videos. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, cystoscopic videos from children with and
papers.summary: This study presents the first AI model to predict vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) in children from cystoscopic images and videos, based on ureteric orifice morphology. The model aims to reduce subjectivity in assessment and could complement or reduce the need for traditional voiding cystourethrography.

papers.title: Lipid Nanoparticles for Gene Therapy: Unresolved Challenges in Manufacturing, Transdermal Delivery, Machine Learning, Endosomal Escape, and the Protein Corona.
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are now the leading delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics, but progress in the field is measured almost entirely by physicochemical and computational proxies rather than by functional properties that determine therapeutic outcomes. This review examines six interconnected areas of LNP development: microfluidic manufacturing, lyophilization, transdermal microneedle delivery, machine learning-guided formulation design, endosomal escape biology, and protein corona-mediated organ targeting. Although these areas are often discussed separately, they are linked by
papers.summary: This review discusses the current state and challenges of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for gene therapy, highlighting six interconnected areas: manufacturing, transdermal delivery, machine learning, endosomal escape, and protein corona. It argues that progress is often measured by physicochemical proxies rather than functional outcomes, and emphasizes the need for a more integrated approach to LNP development.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Prediction of Post-TIPS Outcomes: Integrating Clinical, Biochemical, and Radiomics Data-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is an established treatment for complications of portal hypertension, but hepatic encephalopathy (HE), liver dysfunction, rebleeding, and mortality remain difficult to predict in otherwise eligible candidates. However, predicting post-TIPS outcomes remains challenging using conventional risk scores such as MELD 3.0 and Child-Turcotte-Pugh. This narrative review critically evaluates how clinical, biochemical, procedural, conventional imaging, handcrafted radiomics, and deep-learning features can be integrated for personalized post-TIPS risk p
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly radiomics and deep learning, can improve prediction of outcomes after TIPS procedures for portal hypertension, beyond traditional scores like MELD 3.0. It highlights the potential of integrating clinical, biochemical, and imaging data for personalized risk assessment, though it notes current challenges and the need for further validation.

papers.title: Combining Triazole Scaffold Repurposing and Generative Transformer Architecture for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design Targeting the LasR Quorum Sensing Receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid escalation of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa necessitates anti-virulence strategies targeting quorum sensing rather than bacterial survival; however, integrating scaffold repurposing with generative AI to inhibit LasR remains underexplored. Here, we address this gap by combining triazole scaffold mining with transformer-based de novo molecular generation to systematically identify putative LasR inhibitors. Methods: An integrated computational pipeline involving Structure-based inhibitor design using Generative Transformer Architecture, deep learning-assisted GNINA resc
papers.summary: This study combines triazole scaffold repurposing with a generative transformer architecture to design novel inhibitors of the LasR quorum sensing receptor in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an anti-virulence strategy against multidrug-resistant infections. The integrated computational pipeline, including deep learning-assisted docking rescoring, identified putative LasR inhibitors, demonstrating the potential of combining scaffold mining with generative AI for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: ADS Guard: A Generalizable Defense Framework for Adversarially Robust Occupancy Detection in Smart Buildings.
papers.abstract: Occupancy detection is fundamental to the operational intelligence of smart buildings, driving critical functions in energy management, HVAC automation, and physical security. While modern Deep Learning (DL) models have achieved high accuracy in parsing complex environmental sensor data, they remain highly vulnerable to adversarial examples, imperceptibly perturbed inputs designed to deceive neural networks. These vulnerabilities pose severe real-world risks, ranging from energy sabotage, in which systems heat empty rooms, to critical security breaches in which intruders go undetected. To addr
papers.summary: This paper introduces ADS Guard, a defense framework designed to make deep learning-based occupancy detection in smart buildings robust against adversarial attacks. The framework aims to protect against real-world risks such as energy sabotage and security breaches by generalizing across different attack scenarios.

papers.title: From Descriptor Learning to Binding Stability: An Explainable Machine Learning Pipeline for EGFR Double-Mutant Inhibitor Discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance arising during cancer development and progression remains a major challenge in the treatment of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-driven tumors, particularly those harboring the clinically relevant T790M/L858R double mutation. In this study, we developed an integrated computational workflow combining explainable machine learning, virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding free-energy calculations to identify novel inhibitors of this drug-resistant EGFR variant. An XGBoost regression model was trained using scaffold-aware cross-validation, Bayesian hype
papers.summary: This study presents an explainable machine learning pipeline that integrates XGBoost regression, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and binding free-energy calculations to identify novel inhibitors of the drug-resistant EGFR T790M/L858R double mutant. The approach demonstrates how combining descriptor-based learning with structural validation can efficiently discover candidate compounds with predicted binding stability, offering a practical workflow for targeting resistance mutations in cancer.

papers.title: ERβ-Score: An Interpretable Machine Learning-Based Scoring Function and Web Server for Estrogen Receptor β-Guided Drug Discovery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most clinically aggressive subtype of breast cancer, characterized by the absence of targetable hormone receptors and HER2 amplification, significantly constraining treatment choices. Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) has emerged as a biologically relevant yet underutilized target in TNBC, with its re-expression linked to tumor suppression and improved prognosis, prompting the development of selective ERβ modulators as a precision therapeutic approach. We introduce ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning scoring system developed using a curated datas
papers.summary: The authors developed ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning-based scoring function and web server for predicting ERβ activity, aimed at guiding drug discovery for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The tool leverages a curated dataset to identify potential ERβ modulators, addressing the need for targeted therapies in this aggressive cancer subtype.

papers.title: EFEMP2 Is Associated with Shelterin-Related DNA Damage Repair, Immune Microenvironment Features, and Prognosis in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) carries a median overall survival below 15 months despite aggressive multimodal therapy. Treatment resistance reflects the interplay of genomic instability, dysregulated DNA damage repair (DDR), and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). The shelterin complex maintains telomere integrity, yet its broader role in coordinating DDR, TME remodeling, and clinical outcomes in GBM remains unclear. Methods: We integrated transcriptomic and clinical data from four public cohorts (TCGA, CGGA1, CGGA2, and REMBRANDT, n = 583) and an institutional cohort (CSUXY, n
papers.summary: This study identifies EFEMP2 as a prognostic biomarker in glioblastoma, showing that its expression correlates with shelterin-related DNA damage repair pathways and immune microenvironment features. Using multiple public and institutional cohorts, the authors demonstrate that EFEMP2 is associated with patient survival and may serve as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Culture-Based Microbiological Assessment of Dentin Biomaterials Prepared from Long-Term Refrigerated Human Teeth: A Pilot Study Toward Evidence-Based Tooth Banking.
papers.abstract: Dentin derived from extracted human teeth has emerged as a promising autogenous biomaterial for bone regeneration owing to its structural and biological similarity to bone tissue. Growing clinical interest in dentin-derived graft materials has also stimulated the development of tooth-banking concepts, in which extracted teeth are preserved for future regenerative applications. However, microbiological contamination remains one of the principal concerns associated with long-term storage before clinical use. This in vitro study evaluated the microbiological status of dentin biomaterials prepared
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed the microbiological safety of dentin biomaterials prepared from human teeth stored long-term under refrigeration, finding that the processing method effectively reduced contamination. The results support the feasibility of tooth banking for regenerative dental applications, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Cardiac Sensing: A Bio-Inspired Spiking Neural Network with Sensory-Adaptive Encoding for Energy-Efficient Arrhythmia Detection from ECG and PPG Signals.
papers.abstract: Living nervous systems sense the cardiovascular rhythm with a parsimony that engineered monitors cannot match: sensory receptors encode changes rather than absolute levels, neurons communicate through sparse all-or-none events, retinal circuits sharpen salient features through lateral inhibition, and attention is allocated by surprise. We translate these four principles into BioSpike-Net, a fully event-driven spiking neural network for cardiac-rhythm classification from electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals. A sensory-adaptive spike encoder (SASE) converts analogue wavef
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioSpike-Net, a bio-inspired spiking neural network that applies principles from biological sensory systems (e.g., change encoding, sparse events, lateral inhibition, surprise-based attention) to detect cardiac arrhythmias from ECG and PPG signals. The approach achieves energy-efficient, event-driven classification, potentially enabling low-power wearable cardiac monitoring.

papers.title: Identification of Hub Gene Characteristics and Immune Landscapes Across Aging Subtypes in Atherosclerosis: A Machine Learning-Based Multi-Omics Study With Experimental Verification.
papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for atherosclerosis (AS), but the aging-associated molecular characteristics and immune heterogeneity of AS remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify aging-related hub genes and characterize immune landscapes across aging subtypes of AS using integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. AS-related candidate genes were found by overlapping DEGs identified by limma and key module genes identified by Weighted Correlation Network Analysis (WGCNA) based on the GSE100927 dataset. Consensus clustering based on aging-related DEGs (differential
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and multi-omics approaches to identify aging-related hub genes and characterize immune landscapes across aging subtypes in atherosclerosis, with experimental validation. The findings reveal distinct molecular subtypes and potential biomarkers that could inform personalized treatment strategies for atherosclerosis.

papers.title: Multiclass Machine Learning-Based Discovery of Novel Scaffold Inhibitors Targeting ALK.
papers.abstract: Background: Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK) is an oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase implicated in several cancers. Despite the clinical success of ALK inhibitors, acquired resistance continues to drive the search for novel chemotypes. We developed a multiclass machine learning framework to classify ALK inhibitory activity using a curated ChEMBL dataset. Methods: Models were built using 2D molecular descriptors together with MACCS and ECFP4 fingerprints. Three widely used algorithms, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, were applied for model development. Results: RF
papers.summary: This study developed a multiclass machine learning framework to identify novel ALK inhibitors, using 2D descriptors and fingerprints with SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost on a curated ChEMBL dataset. The Random Forest model performed best, enabling the discovery of new scaffold inhibitors that could overcome resistance.

papers.title: FluEvoFormer: A Structure-Guided Generative Foundation Model for Prospective Influenza Antigenic Evolution and Vaccine Strain Selection.
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccine strain selection remains challenging because circulating viruses may drift after vaccine recommendations are made. This study presents FluEvoFormer, a structure-guided generative foundation model for prospective influenza antigenic evolution forecasting and vaccine strain ranking. The framework jointly encodes hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences and incorporates residue-contact graphs. Separate prediction heads estimate future viral dominance and the vaccine-virus antigenic match. Controlled future-like variant stress testing, uncertainty adjustments, and clade
papers.summary: FluEvoFormer is a new structure-guided generative model that predicts future influenza antigenic evolution and ranks vaccine strains by jointly encoding hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences with residue-contact graphs. It uses separate prediction heads for viral dominance and vaccine-virus antigenic match, and includes stress testing and uncertainty adjustments to improve prospective accuracy. This could help make seasonal vaccine strain selection more reliable.

papers.title: PepGen: conditional generation of peptides for MHC binding.
papers.abstract: Peptide-MHC II binding drives adaptive immunity, yet discovery of novel binder peptides remains challenging due to open binding grooves of MHC-II that accommodate variable-length peptides. While discriminative models perform well, they are unfeasible for generation via enumeration due to vast peptide space (2013≈8×1016 for peptides of length 13 amino acids). Generative AI approaches could accelerate binder design to enable vaccines targeted to particular MHC-II alleles or optimize other peptide chemical properties.
papers.summary: PepGen is a new generative AI tool that directly designs peptide sequences predicted to bind specific MHC-II alleles, overcoming the impracticality of enumerating the vast peptide sequence space. This approach could accelerate the development of targeted vaccines and allow optimization of other peptide properties.

papers.title: Pocket-PROTACs: an interpretable pocket-aware deep learning framework for predicting PROTAC-induced protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation by recruiting an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a protein of interest (POI) and forming a ternary complex. Despite their therapeutic promise, rational PROTAC design remains challenging, as degradation efficacy depends on subtle and highly structure-dependent interactions among the POI, the E3 ligase, and the bifunctional molecule.
papers.summary: This paper presents Pocket-PROTACs, an interpretable deep learning framework that predicts PROTAC-induced protein degradation by analyzing the binding pockets of the target protein and E3 ligase. The model captures structure-dependent ternary complex interactions, offering a tool for rational PROTAC design.

papers.title: RIBEX: predicting and explaining RNA binding across structured and intrinsically disordered regions (IDR)-rich proteins.
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate post-transcriptional processes, yet many remain undiscovered because RNA-binding activity often occurs outside canonical RNA-binding domains (RBDs), including within intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) or through protein complexes. Computational methods can help identify novel RBPs, but approaches relying solely on sequence-derived features or ignoring the cellular interaction context are limited in capturing the complexity of RNA-binding behavior. To date, no framework rigorously integrates both sequence information and protein interaction context for
papers.summary: RIBEX is a new computational framework that predicts RNA-binding proteins by integrating both sequence-derived features and protein interaction context, addressing the challenge of identifying RNA-binding activity outside canonical domains, including in intrinsically disordered regions. It provides explainable predictions, which could help discover novel RBPs and improve understanding of post-transcriptional regulation.

papers.title: Stoic: fast and accurate protein stoichiometry prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes are central to cellular function, but experimental determination of their structures remains challenging. Structure prediction methods require prior knowledge of stoichiometry-the number of copies of each protein entity within a complex. Current approaches rely on computationally expensive brute-force methods that run structure prediction on multiple stoichiometry combinations, often with limited accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Stoic, a fast and accurate tool for predicting protein complex stoichiometry, which is a prerequisite for structure prediction. It addresses the computational bottleneck of brute-force approaches by providing a more efficient method, potentially improving the accuracy of downstream complex structure modeling.

papers.title: Red blood cell distribution width is associated with coronary artery disease in latent tuberculosis infection: a machine learning-based study.
papers.abstract: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) is associated with an increased risk of coronary artery disease (CAD), potentially mediated by systemic inflammation. Traditional lipid-based risk models may have limited predictive performance in tuberculosis-affected populations.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to investigate whether red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients with latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI). The findings suggest that RDW, a marker of inflammation, may improve CAD risk prediction in this population beyond traditional lipid-based models.

papers.title: Plasma proteomics reveals the molecular features in rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis.
papers.abstract: Rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis (RPP) is an aggressive subtype of pneumoconiosis characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation, rapidly progressive fibrosis, and early-onset progressive massive fibrosis. However, the systemic molecular alterations of RPP remain unclear. Here, we profiled the plasma proteome to identify candidate proteins associated with RPP, aiming to discover potential peripheral biomarkers for this aggressive phenotype.
papers.summary: This study profiles the plasma proteome of patients with rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis (RPP) to identify molecular features and potential peripheral biomarkers distinguishing this aggressive subtype. The findings reveal candidate proteins associated with RPP, offering insights into systemic alterations and potential diagnostic targets.

papers.title: An evaluation based on explainable machine learning: analysis of risk factors for enteral nutrition-related diarrhea in patients with severe stroke.
papers.abstract: This study systematically examines the clinical factors associated with enteral nutrition-related diarrhea (ENAD) in patients with severe stroke and uses interpretable machine learning methods to assess the strength of these associations.
papers.summary: This study uses explainable machine learning to identify and rank clinical risk factors for enteral nutrition-related diarrhea in severe stroke patients, providing interpretable insights for clinical decision-making. The approach highlights key modifiable factors that could guide preventive strategies in intensive care settings.

papers.title: Exploration of acetylation-related biomarkers in osteoarthritis through bioinformatics analysis.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is characterized as a chronic degenerative disorder affecting the joints. A growing body of evidence indicates that acetylation may play a role in the disease's pathogenesis. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely undefined. The objective of this study was to explore potential biomarkers linked to acetylation in OA through a comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. We utilized datasets GSE55235, GSE55457, and GSE12021 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) by employing the limma package, followed by functi
papers.summary: This study uses public gene expression datasets to identify acetylation-related biomarkers in osteoarthritis, finding differentially expressed genes that may serve as diagnostic or therapeutic targets. The work provides a bioinformatics-based exploration of acetylation's role in OA pathogenesis, though the findings are preliminary and require experimental validation.

papers.title: A structure and function-based complete mutational map of human hemoglobin using AI.
papers.abstract: Hemoglobin (Hb), a well-characterized protein central to oxygen transport and molecular medicine, serves as a model for studying how sequence variations influence protein structure and function. Its precise activity depends on tightly regulated structural dynamics, which can be disrupted by mutations that give rise to structural hemoglobinopathies, including sickle cell disease, unstable hemoglobins, methemoglobins, and hemoglobins with altered oxygen affinity, each associated with distinct functional and clinical consequences. Among genetic variants, missense mutations are the most widely stu
papers.summary: This study uses AI to generate a complete mutational map of human hemoglobin, linking sequence variations to structural and functional consequences. It provides a comprehensive resource for understanding how missense mutations cause hemoglobinopathies like sickle cell disease and altered oxygen affinity.

papers.title: Explicit encoding of temporal dynamics for interpretable melody similarity modeling: insight into machine learning models.
papers.abstract: Temporal melody similarity is a fundamental problem in music modelling, and current methods are mostly based on recurrent or attention-based architectures that implicitly learn sequential structures.
papers.summary: This paper proposes an explicit encoding of temporal dynamics for melody similarity modeling, offering interpretability compared to implicit recurrent or attention-based approaches. The work provides insight into how machine learning models can capture sequential structure in music, potentially improving both performance and understanding.

papers.title: MetaCYP: a unified framework for prediction of cytochrome P450 metabolic sites and reaction types via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are the predominant drug-metabolizing proteins in humans, collectively governing the structural transformation of drugs and xenobiotics while directly shaping their pharmacological activity and toxicological profiles. Accurate prediction of CYP-substrate reaction sites and reaction types is therefore central to drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment. Existing computational models, however, largely depend on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, constraining their generalization across CYP isoforms.
papers.summary: MetaCYP is a new deep learning framework that predicts both the metabolic sites and reaction types for cytochrome P450 enzymes, addressing limitations of existing models that rely on molecular properties or fixed rules. It uses multimodal learning to improve generalization across different CYP isoforms, which is important for drug discovery and safety assessment.

papers.title: Peripheral endocrine-nutritional machine learning signature predicts short-term response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Major pathological response (MPR) to neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) varies widely and is incompletely explained by tumor-side biomarkers. Because checkpoint inhibitors act within a host environment shaped by endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory state, we developed and validated the Endocrine-Nutritional Immunotherapy response score (ENI-Score) from routine pretreatment peripheral-blood markers to predict short-term response and early recurrence.
papers.summary: The authors developed and validated a machine learning-based score (ENI-Score) using routine pretreatment peripheral-blood markers related to endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory status to predict short-term response (major pathological response) and early recurrence in patients with locally advanced gastric cancer receiving neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy. The score aims to complement tumor-side biomarkers by capturing host systemic factors that influence checkpoint inhibitor efficacy.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), revealing its association with vascular-immune crosstalk and its potential as a prognostic biomarker. The findings suggest EMCN could serve as a novel therapeutic target or diagnostic marker for LUAD.

papers.title: Identification and validation of key host genes associated with porcine H1N1 infection based on integrated machine learning algorithms.
papers.abstract: Swine H1N1 influenza is a critical zoonotic pathogen threatening pig industry economy and public health. The host molecular regulatory network and core genes of H1N1 infection remain unclear, hindering targeted prevention and therapy. Traditional experimental methods fail to efficiently mine high-dimensional transcriptomic data, making precise screening of infection biomarkers difficult. Methods: Transcriptome data (GSE40092) were analyzed to obtain porcine lung DEGs upon H1N1 infection, followed by GO/KEGG functional enrichment. Four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE,
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning on porcine lung transcriptomic data to identify key host genes associated with H1N1 influenza infection, providing potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. The integrated approach highlights the utility of computational methods for mining high-dimensional data in infectious disease research.

papers.title: Cross-residual knowledge graph learning for robust multi-trait gene-trait prioritization in rice.
papers.abstract: Prioritizing genes associated with agronomic traits remains challenging because relevant evidence is distributed across heterogeneous biological resources and curated gene-trait associations are incomplete.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational method that uses a knowledge graph to integrate heterogeneous biological data and prioritize genes linked to agronomic traits in rice, even when curated gene-trait associations are incomplete. The approach, called cross-residual knowledge graph learning, improves the robustness of gene prioritization by leveraging cross-residual connections across different data types, offering a more reliable way to identify candidate genes for crop improvement.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Pathogenic LMNA Missense Variants: Structural Instability, Altered Binding, and Conformational Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the LMNA gene underlie a broad spectrum of laminopathies, including muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and premature aging syndromes; however, the molecular mechanisms by which missense variants disrupt Lamin A structural integrity remain incompletely characterized. Systematic computational approaches for prioritizing pathogenic variants and elucidating their structural consequences are critically needed.
papers.summary: This study computationally characterizes pathogenic missense variants in the LMNA gene, which cause laminopathies, by assessing structural instability, altered protein binding, and conformational dynamics. The findings provide a systematic framework for prioritizing pathogenic variants and understanding their molecular consequences.

papers.title: InfoMedex: drug-drug interaction prediction via a multimodal CNN-transformer model.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions are an important source of preventable adverse drug events. Computational methods that incorporate chemical structure and biological context may support more scalable and interpretable interaction prediction.
papers.journal: Frontiers in drug safety and regulation
papers.summary: This paper introduces InfoMedex, a multimodal deep learning model that combines convolutional neural networks and transformers to predict drug-drug interactions using both chemical structure and biological context. The model aims to provide a more scalable and interpretable approach to identifying potential adverse drug events, which could improve drug safety screening.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-integrated multimodal retinal imaging for early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: We developed and validated RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework for simultaneous risk stratification of hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative-associated retinal changes from integrated fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata.
papers.summary: The authors developed RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata to simultaneously assess risk for hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative retinal changes. The model aims to enable early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases through retinal imaging.

papers.title: OtoVCE: a mechanism-aware language-model evidence layer for hereditary hearing-loss variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in genes implicated in hereditary hearing loss are frequently returned to clinicians as variants of uncertain significance. In silico predictors and rule-based ACMG/AMP frameworks each capture only a fraction of the required evidence, and neither directly accesses case-level and functional evidence reported in the published literature.
papers.summary: OtoVCE is a new tool that uses a language model to automatically extract and interpret evidence from the published literature for hereditary hearing-loss missense variants, integrating this with existing predictors and ACMG/AMP rules. It aims to reduce the number of variants of uncertain significance by providing a more comprehensive evidence layer for clinicians.

papers.title: The Embodied Hijack: when Pleistocene minds meet disembodied artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has intensified a long-standing feature of human cognition: the attribution of agency, intention, and understanding to nonhuman systems. People describe language models, virtual assistants, and autonomous technologies as if these systems know, decide, want, or understand, and they continue to do so even when they know the systems have no inner life. The standard account dismisses this as naïve anthropomorphism, the misfiring of evolved agency-detection systems calibrated in the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness. We argue
papers.summary: This paper argues that attributing agency and intention to AI systems is not simply a cognitive error but a deeply rooted feature of human cognition shaped by Pleistocene evolution. The authors propose that our evolved agency-detection systems, calibrated for social environments, are 'hijacked' by disembodied AI, leading people to treat these systems as intentional agents even when they know otherwise.

papers.title: SHAP-interpretable machine learning integrating exposures and multi-omics reveals immune alterations and biomarkers in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) frequently co-occur and share environmental and biological determinants, yet their cross-scale associations remain incompletely understood. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based integration of exposome and multi-omics data provide new opportunities for dissecting this complex comorbidity.
papers.summary: This study uses SHAP-interpretable machine learning to integrate exposure and multi-omics data, revealing immune alterations and identifying biomarkers associated with COPD-lung cancer comorbidity. The approach provides new insights into the cross-scale biological mechanisms linking these two diseases.
